target_customer: Brazilian startups and SMBs with a CNPJ
problem: Brazilian companies lacked a single account combining business banking, corporate cards and expense control.
business_model: Interchange and fees on corporate cards and accounts plus SaaS expense management and credit

founders.name: Ricardo Gottschalk
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Sales Manager at Creditas, BD manager at Stone Pagamentos, and a sales rep role at Oracle (spelled Oralce).

founders.name: Fernando Santos
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; 16 plus years in software including client work for Bradesco and Santander.

technical_complexity.rationale: Core banking via a licensed partner plus card issuing, expense workflows and ERP integrations; standard fintech engineering with integration and compliance work.

defensibility.rationale: Accounts and cards embedded in finance workflows are sticky and need licences or partner banks, but features can be copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Nubank Business and Cora offer business accounts and Clara later launched a PJ account; per a latamfintech article, none removed the company, which reached breakeven in October 2023.

market_need_then: Brazil had many SMBs underserved by traditional banks; the company cites over 50,000 clients later. Contemporary 2020 demand evidence was not found in sources opened.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simplicity positioning; the 2.0 campaign centres on simplified complexity.

branding.brand_signature: No meu tempo brand campaign for the smart card (April)

brand_strength.rationale: Funded brand campaigns and a CMO hire are reported by marketing trade outlets; no community or virality evidence.

outcome_analysis: Conta Simples raised a Series A of R$121.4M in December 2021 and a $41.5M Series B in January 2024 led by Base10, after reaching breakeven in October 2023. It serves tens of thousands of companies per its own claims. It is active and growing, with a credit licence and acquisition of Hackr Ads in 2022 reported by one secondary source.
notes: Series A was R$121.4M; no USD figure stated so amount_usd is null. The Series B valuation was not disclosed (sources conflict on a multiple of the prior round). Competitor list left empty: 2020-dated sources were not found; named later competitors (Clara, Cora, Nubank) came from undated or later articles. Founding year 2019 comes from a secondary latamfintech article.
